scope: Workplace / supply GHS–CLP classification, not transport or substance-specific hazard determination.

eu.note: No single UN GHS revision describes the law: CLP selectively incorporates GHS changes through amendments and also has EU-only hazard classes (EU 2023/707). Check the current consolidated text and any later ATP application dates.

eea.note: The EEA framework uses EU CLP; later amendments may require EEA incorporation and specific entry-into-force checks. Do not simply assume all EU or Swiss application dates are identical.

gb.note: GB CLP derives from EU CLP as assimilated and amended under GB law, rather than adopting one fixed GHS revision. EU changes after Brexit do not automatically apply in GB.

ni.note: Northern Ireland uses EU CLP (not the GB MCL regime). Follow EU CLP revisions, relevant ATP application dates and the Windsor Framework arrangements.

ch.note: No single UN GHS revision: Switzerland adopts selected changes through Swiss chemicals legislation. EU-derived endocrine disruption, PBT/vPvB and PMT/vPvM classes have Swiss-specific dates: binding for substances from 1 Nov 2026 and for mixtures from 1 May 2028.

tr.note: Türkiye operates an EU CLP-derived national SEA classification scheme. A precise single UN GHS revision could not be established reliably for all amendments; use the current Turkish annexes and official text.

my.note: DOSH guidance explicitly references the third revised edition and requires the precautionary statements specified in the ICOP rather than substituting those from GHS Revision 4. Review the applicable CLASS and ICOP text.

kr.note: Industry regulatory commentary maps MoEL Notice 2025-50 to GHS Revision 4; the official ministry source confirms the 2025 notice, but a current official statement of the revision number was not verified. Check the regulation and separate NICS schedules.

cn.note: China does not use one uniform revision: GB 30000.2–29:2013 hazard standards derive from GHS Rev 4; GB 30000.1:2024 general rules reference Rev 8 (effective Aug 2025); GB 30000.30:2025 introduced desensitised explosives from July 2026 and references Rev 10. Newer updates must be checked standard-by-standard.

nz.note: Based on GHS Rev 7, effective from 30 April 2021, with expressly excluded optional categories and additional terrestrial ecotoxicity hazards limited to relevant agrichemicals.

au.note: GHS Rev 7 is mandatory for new workplace classifications and SDSs from 1 January 2023, subject to legacy-stock labelling provisions. Some optional GHS categories are not adopted, and environmental classes are outside the workplace hazardous-chemical definition.

jp.note: The revised JIS Z 7252:2025 and Z 7253:2025 published 25 December 2025 adopt Rev 9; NITE provides both Rev 6/JIS 2019 and Rev 9/JIS 2025 tools during a five-year transition. Verify which version and sector-specific duties apply.

ca.note: Hazardous Products Regulations adopted Rev 7, plus Chemicals Under Pressure from Rev 8. The three-year general transition ended 14 Dec 2025. National compliance/enforcement communications should be checked for subsequent operational arrangements.

us.note: The 2024 HCS primarily aligns with Rev 7 and adds selected elements from later revisions; OSHA extended 2024 HCS compliance dates on 15 Jan 2026. Some transition options remain; consult the current OSHA timeline. OSHA excludes environmental hazards from mandatory workplace classification.

br.note: The revised ABNT NBR 14725:2023 is reported as Rev 7-aligned and effective 4 July 2025. Verify the latest ABNT technical standard and applicable NR-26 obligations (the full standard may require purchase).

mx.note: The official Mexican standard explicitly states that it is partially equivalent to GHS Fifth Revised Edition (2013), with national modifications. Workplace scheme does not implement the environmental hazard classes as mandatory NOM-018 classifications.

sg.note: Singapore adopted revised SS 586 parts 2 and 3 for applicable controls from 6 Feb 2025. Official public product summaries do not clearly establish one UN GHS revision for all national adaptations; verify the actual standard before assigning a revision number.

za.note: South African Hazardous Chemical Agents Regulations refer to the latest GHS, and note that SANS 10234:2019 may differ from the GHS Purple Book. Accordingly a single numeric edition cannot be safely assigned without reviewing current binding amendments and relevant standards.

hazards.description: GHS physical hazard class.

hazards.label: Acute toxicity — categories 1–4
hazards.description: Includes oral, dermal and inhalation routes.

hazards.label: Acute toxicity — category 5
hazards.description: Optional lower-severity category not adopted by many major workplace schemes.

hazards.label: Skin corrosion — category 1
hazards.description: Includes jurisdiction-specific subdivisions 1A/1B/1C where recognised.

hazards.label: Skin irritation — category 2
hazards.description: Standard skin irritation category.

hazards.label: Skin irritation — category 3
hazards.description: Optional mild irritation category, not part of EU CLP or NZ system.

hazards.label: Serious eye damage — category 1
hazards.description: Severe eye damage (e.g., H318).

hazards.label: Eye irritation — category 2 / 2A
hazards.description: See eye irritation 2B and any combined Category 2 separately.

hazards.label: Eye irritation — category 2B separately
hazards.description: Some schemes use 2B; others combine 2A and 2B under Category 2.

hazards.label: Respiratory sensitisation
hazards.description: May be subdivided according to the national regime.

hazards.label: Skin sensitisation
hazards.description: May be subdivided into 1A/1B.

hazards.label: Germ-cell mutagenicity
hazards.description: Categories and subdivisions may vary.

hazards.label: Carcinogenicity
hazards.description: Hazard classification, distinct from list-based IARC duties.

hazards.label: Reproductive toxicity
hazards.description: Including effects on or via lactation when applicable.

hazards.label: STOT — single exposure
hazards.description: Specific target organ toxicity, including Category 3 effects.

hazards.label: STOT — repeated exposure
hazards.description: Specific target organ toxicity from repeated exposures.

hazards.label: Aspiration hazard — category 1
hazards.description: Aspiration hazard Category 1.

hazards.label: Aspiration hazard — category 2
hazards.description: Optional lower-severity category not adopted in many schemes.

hazards.label: Aquatic acute — category 1
hazards.description: Short-term aquatic hazards.

hazards.label: Aquatic acute — categories 2 and 3
hazards.description: Optional acute aquatic categories that some countries exclude.

hazards.label: Aquatic chronic — categories 1–4
hazards.description: Long-term aquatic hazard categories; exact subcategories can differ.

hazards.label: Hazardous to the ozone layer
hazards.description: A separate environmental hazard class.

hazards.label: Endocrine disruption — human health
hazards.description: EU 2023/707 class with categories 1 and 2 (EUH380 / EUH381).

hazards.label: Endocrine disruption — environment
hazards.description: EU 2023/707 class with categories 1 and 2 (EUH430 / EUH431).

hazards.label: PBT / vPvB
hazards.description: EU-only chemical persistence / bioaccumulation hazard classes (EUH440 / EUH441).

hazards.label: PMT / vPvM
hazards.description: EU-only persistence / mobility hazard classes (EUH450 / EUH451).

hazards.label: Terrestrial ecotoxicity — NZ-specific
hazards.description: NZ-specific categories for certain agrichemicals and active ingredients; not UN GHS.

hazards.label: Combustible dust — additional workplace hazard
hazards.description: US and Canadian workplace hazard beyond the base GHS class scheme.

hazards.label: Simple asphyxiant — additional workplace hazard
hazards.description: US and Canadian workplace hazard beyond base GHS.
